full_description:
Join CoolRater’s winter 2026–27 field trial of a Windows app that measures the Heat-Transfer Coefficient of your home, a statistic used to support heat-pump sizing. Participants will install the app, connect an Octopus Energy account, provide half-hourly smart-meter data, and collect overnight temperatures using four Elitech RC-5+ loggers, which will be provided. Applicants must heat their home with a gas boiler and avoid using energy outside the home during trial sessions. Basic computer skills are sufficient; CSV editing and installing unsigned trial software are required. Five participants are sought each month from November 2026 to February 2027.

CoolRater is a desktop app which will measure the heat transfer coefficient HTC for a building, a function that has become increasingly important in recent years for use in sizing heat pumps. A field trial is being run this winter with these objectives:

1. To obtain temperature and energy data for a range of properties. Currently CoolRater has only been used for the author’s own property.

2. to obtain data from properties where the temperature varies between locations due to variations in insulation or heat distribution. For example close to a solid floor with no insulation, or in rooms which do not have double glazing.

3. To find out if users have any problems in using the app, or have any dislikes or need for additional features or improvements.

There are some specific requirements for participants:

1. The app only supports Windows (10 or 11);
2. heating must be with a gas boiler;
3. your energy supplier must be Octopus Energy, and you must be able to connect to the Octopus API, which means that you will have to live in the UK.
4. you must have a smart meter, configured to record energy use every 30 minutes. As a quick check that the smart meter and API is working correctly, there is a feature on the Octopus website where you can download smart meter data. Log in to your Octopus account, click your name top right, click My Energy, scroll down to "Get your energy geek on" you can download files of energy usage. Please download two days of energy data and attach it to your proposal, so that I can see that you have a working smart meter.
5. during the trial, which is only active at night, you will not be able to use energy for anything outside the house, like charging EVs.

To collect the temperature data you will be provided with four Elitech RC-5+ logging thermometers. To send you these, I will need your address. Exchanging contact details is discouraged by PPH rules, but is allowed after a proposal has been accepted if it is necessary to mail equipment. Note that a similar project is also posted which differs only in that participants buy their own thermometers, receive a higher amount as a result, and do not therefore need to provide their address.

A high level of computer expertise is not required but you will need to copy your API key from your Octopus account to the app, you may need to edit CSV files with Excel or LibraOffice, and install the app. As trial software it has not been possible to digitally sign it and it has had few downloads. Therefore the operating system will treat it with suspicion and advise you not to run it. You can run it against this advice by clicking “More Information” and “Run Anyway”.

The video [login to view URL] gives instructions on using the app and shows what you will need to do as a participant in the field trial.

Criteria for Job Completion

As trial software its difficult to be certain of how well it will work. The app calculates the HTC for each inside thermometer by three different methods. If for any one of the thermometers the results agree to within 10%, then jobs a good’un. If they don’t, then this often indicates a problem with the thermometer being close to a heating source. So I would like you to repeat the test one or two times to get a better result. Return either one project file with the results agreeing to within 10%, or three project files from three separate attempts.

It is intended that there will be five participants in each of the months November 2026 to February 2027.

Summary
I am seeking an experienced developmental editor and beta reader specializing in creative non-fiction and memoirs to help restructure, tighten, and elevate the narrative momentum of my completed 90,000-word manuscript, Against the Weight of Numbers.

About the Book:
Written through the dry, self-deprecating lens of a Bengaluru-based IT systems engineer and delivery manager, this memoir contrasts twenty years of managing complex corporate infrastructure and SLAs against an unmonitored, life-threatening biological collapse.

The narrative tracks my ascent past 200 kilograms, the moment a digital bathroom scale flashed an Err code, an October 2025 respiratory emergency (55% SpO2) where a standard ambulance could not accommodate my frame—forcing my personal SUV to act as an emergency transport rig to the ICU—followed by 17 days on life support, severe Mounjaro-induced sarcopenia (a 2:00 AM washroom collapse), and a data-driven physical rebuild back to 8,000 daily steps.

The Editorial Challenge (What I Need From You):
Two publishing professionals have reviewed the opening chapters and synopsis and identified two specific structural issues that I want to solve before submitting to the next wave of literary agents:

Length & Compression: At 90,000 words, the manuscript is too long for a debut memoir. 

Novelistic Pacing & Opening Hook: Currently, the opening chapters unfold chronologically (childhood, engineering college, early IT career) as a series of standalone comedic anecdotes before the medical stakes arrive much later. I want to re-architect the opening—likely using an in-media-res hook—to create immediate "what happens next?" tension while preserving my dry humor and Indian/Hinglish conversational rhythm.

Deliverables Expected:

A comprehensive Editorial Letter / Structural Roadmap (chapter-by-chapter breakdown of what to cut, merge, move, or rewrite).

In-manuscript margin comments flagging pacing drags, repetitive reflections ("telling instead of showing"), and structural transitions.

A 1-hour follow-up call to discuss your feedback and align on the revision plan.

(Note: I am looking for structural/developmental editing only—not line/copy editing.)
